sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kubra Fatima
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned for the applicant, Shri M. Hasan, Advocate holding brief of learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of applicant is taken on record.
Supplementary counter affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent no.2 and counter affidavit filed by learned A.G.A. are taken on record.
3. In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that the sister of the informant was missing.

Subsequently,
because of the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that the applicant had enticed her on the false pretext of marriage and thereafter committed wrong on her.
During trial, the victim has turned hostile and not supported the prosecution story.

Hence, the applicant who is languishing Yashpal vs State Of Up Thru. Prin. Secy. Home And ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152939074/
1 in jail since 27.7.2023 and the applicant has no criminal history, hence he may be released on bail.

entities.text: Yashpal vs State Of Up Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the fact that the victim has not supported the prosecution story during trial and turned hostile coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 27.7.2023 and has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Yashpal be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.475 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Dhaurhara, District Lakhimpur Kheri on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.4.2024 Shukla  Yashpal vs State Of Up Thru. Prin. Secy.
